title: Certified Fidelity Susceptibility from Classical Shadows
abstract: Fidelity susceptibility is a useful probe of quantum phase transitions and quantum metrology, but its direct evaluation on a quantum device is challenging. By integrating Krylov-subspace methods with a resolvent-based reformulation, we present a method for certifying fidelity susceptibility using randomized single-copy measurements across repeated ground-state preparations. The resulting approximations form monotone lower bounds to the exact fidelity susceptibility and converge geometrically. We also present applications to metrology and linear static susceptibilities.

bite.hook: New randomized single-copy measurement method certifies quantum fidelity susceptibility via monotone lower bounds.
tldr: Presented a method for certifying fidelity susceptibility on quantum devices.
Integrated Krylov-subspace methods with a resolvent-based reformulation using randomized single-copy measurements.
Proved that the resulting approximations form monotone lower bounds that converge geometrically.
bite.whyItMatters: Fidelity susceptibility helps scientists spot quantum phase transitions and improve quantum sensors, but it is notoriously difficult to calculate directly on quantum hardware. This technique makes evaluating it much more practical.
bite.eli5: Checking how fragile a quantum state is usually requires impossibly complicated measurements. This new trick lets scientists take simple, random snapshots of the system to safely estimate its sensitivity.
